title: MetroForge
author: Senior_Platypus_2694
selftext:
🚇 MetroForge Development Update — September 2026

MetroForge has come a long way from being just an idea.

The goal is ambitious: build an AI-powered system capable of generating complete, playable Metroidvania-style games — world structure, rooms, characters, enemies, bosses, mechanics, progression, assets, animations, UI, audio, Godot projects, testing, and eventually shipping builds.

And a lot of that infrastructure is now real.

Recent testing has proven that MetroForge can generate complete Godot projects, import them into Godot, run gameplay systems, and export standalone builds. Earlier AI-generation tests also successfully produced real NVIDIA/FLUX character and creature source artwork, which was processed into game-ready assets.

The asset pipeline has grown substantially as well. It now supports characters, environments, animated environments, VFX, UI panels, animation metadata, SpriteFrames compilation, palette/cohesion validation, tileset checks, provenance, QA, and production-readiness gates.

One of the latest pipeline rehearsals successfully exercised 27 assets and 18 animations, with the focused regression suite passing 52/52 tests.

But MetroForge isn't at the finish line yet.

The current major challenge is real production-quality asset generation on the hardware available to the project. The latest OpenVINO production attempt timed out while generating the first 384×384 asset, so I am not counting that run as a successful production generation.

That's important because I don't want MetroForge to call something "production ready" just because a pipeline completed.

The standard I'm working toward is much higher:

Prompt → Game Design → World → Assets → Gameplay → Godot → Automated QA → Playable Game → Export

with actual evidence at every stage.

There has already been real visual/runtime progress. Previous MetroForge validation produced runtime gameplay captures, tileset assembly previews and asset contact sheets, while Godot import/runtime and the visual harness passed during that visual-validation work.

Earlier AI-generation testing also produced a real 377,782-byte NVIDIA FLUX player source image, along with 5 NVIDIA-generated source assets and 77 game-ready assets derived through the pixel-art processing pipeline.

So the project is in an interesting position:

The architecture is becoming serious.

The game-generation pipeline is real.

Godot generation and runtime have been demonstrated.

AI asset generation has been demonstrated.

Production-scale visual consistency and reliable local generation are the next major barriers.

I'm building MetroForge around one rule:

If the evidence doesn't prove it works, MetroForge doesn't get to claim that it works.

Still building. Still testing. Still closing gaps.

The destination is a system where you describe the Metroidvania you want — and MetroForge builds the game.
